g.title: g-delta-uq builds principle stochastic anchoring each input sample transformed relative representation subtracting randomly chosen anchor concatenating channel-wise producing anchored input
g.desc: G-Delta-UQ builds on the principle of stochastic anchoring. Each input sample is transformed into a relative representation by subtracting a randomly chosen anchor and concatenating it channel-wise, producing an anchored input.
g.text: Pick a random anchor, subtract it and concatenate
channel-wise to form a relative "anchored input":
anchored(x) = [ x − c , c ] with random anchor c

g.title: varying anchor across iterations model emulates sampling distribution hypotheses variance predictions multiple anchors captures epistemic uncertainty
g.desc: By varying the anchor across iterations, the model emulates sampling from a distribution of hypotheses, and the variance of predictions over multiple anchors captures epistemic uncertainty.
g.text: Changing the anchor across iterations emulates
sampling from a distribution of hypotheses.
The variance of predictions over many anchors

g.title: because directly anchoring graph adjacency introduce artificial edges authors anchor node-feature hidden-representation space three variants node features intermediate message-passing layer after readout
g.desc: Because directly anchoring on graph adjacency would introduce artificial edges, the authors anchor in node-feature or hidden-representation space. They introduce three variants, applying anchoring at the node features, at an intermediate message-passing layer, or after the readout.
g.text: THREE ANCHORING VARIANTS (Figure 2) — anchor in feature / hidden space, never adjacency
Anchoring adjacency would add fake edges, so anchor at the node features, an intermediate
message-passing layer, or after readout — inducing different levels of stochasticity.

g.title: particularly practical variant freezes pretrained backbone only trains anchored classifier head inexpensive partial stochasticity inference predictions averaged over K anchors calibrated prediction uncertainty estimate
g.desc: A particularly practical variant freezes a pretrained backbone and only trains an anchored classifier head, delivering inexpensive, partial stochasticity. At inference, predictions are averaged over K anchors to produce both a calibrated prediction and an uncertainty estimate.
g.text: over K anchors to get both:
